newsitem.title: FRANCE: Need for soup kitchens seen rising in France.
newsitem.headline: Need for soup kitchens seen rising in France.

text.p: French soup kitchen volunteers launched their annual campaign on Monday and said they expected rising demand for free meals from more homeless and destitute people during the winter.

"We provided 50 million meals last year, but there is so much poverty in France that we fear we might reach 60 million this year," said Marie Dumas, president of the "Restos du Coeur" (Restaurants of the Heart), founded by the late popular comic Coluche in 1985.
The group, helped by artists and entertainment figures, handed out 8.5 million meals in its first campaign 11 years ago. It is financed by donations and European Union subisidies.

"Sometimes, we wonder if we shouldn't stop to let people realise just how much poverty there is in this country," said Dumas, who will rely this year on a nationwide network of 1,500 centres of distribution served by some 30,000 volunteers.
"The fact that we are starting our 12th campaign does not mean that we're successful, only that too many people need us," Dumas added.
Coluche ran for president in 1986 but pulled out before the poll. He died a few months later in a motorcycle crash.
